subject.title: fix: harden browser media and remote CLI attachments

question: Should remote asset URL summaries fail closed for CLI providers that require broad local tool approval, even though that can stop existing Claude/Gemini-style remote attachment workflows?
rationale: The patch deliberately trades compatibility for a stricter SSRF/confused-deputy boundary, and that policy choice should remain maintainer-owned even though the code path is narrow.

options.title: Accept the fail-closed security boundary
options.body: Merge the documented restriction so untrusted remote assets cannot expand into broad local CLI tool access.

options.title: Preserve compatibility behind explicit opt-in
options.body: Add a clearly named unsafe/legacy opt-in before merge if maintainers need the old remote CLI behavior for known environments.

options.title: Pause for provider-specific migration
options.body: Hold the PR if maintainers want each affected CLI provider to gain a safer attachment path before blocking the old behavior.

recommendation.title: Accept the fail-closed security boundary
recommendation.body: Merge the documented restriction so untrusted remote assets cannot expand into broad local CLI tool access.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete owns the recent browser media, browser URL guard, and asset CLI flow history and authored the security-boundary change.
